question: Does the newer Strata (and the hokar3361 fork) improve tok/s vs our v0.1.39 install?

fork_analysis.change: ONE Metal/macOS-only patch: wrap >maxBufferLength (41.75 GB M4 Max) model files in multiple no-copy Metal buffers so IQ3_XXS can be arena-resident on a 64 GB Mac (metal/src/mtl_rt.mm, window.cpp, prompt_chain.inc moe_rebase)
fork_analysis.verdict_for_borg: NO benefit - the code path is Metal-only. Linux/ROCm/gfx1201 cannot use it. The fork's value for us is only that it points at upstream v0.1.44.

ab_test.host: borg, R9700 gfx1201, Strata engine, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, shared-expert-arena, 262144 ctx, k8v4
ab_test.method: same probe on both builds: 5x 256-token decode (median) + 46.8K-token prefill; live v0.1.39 on :8080, new build on :8081; identical config + hipBLASLt tuning table
notes: First-pass numbers (decode 70, prefill 899->1399) were optimistic; 5-run medians are the figures above.
178K prefill samples seen in logs are prefix-cache hits (repeated prompt), not real prefill - excluded.
--adapt-async is not present in our v0.1.39 engine help; it arrives with the newer build. Matches upstream's claimed +4-5% decode.
v0.1.44 also carries the #771 THP-wedge fix (0.1.40) and hung-engine detection (0.1.41).

recommendation: Upgrade the live flashnext service to the v0.1.44 binary + --adapt-async 1 (~+22% decode, ~+29% prefill). Do NOT install the hokar3361 fork (Metal-only).
